feature: One worktree per feature (slug), local main as the only destination
gating: Run layers in order. Do not run a layer until every case in the layer before it passes.

unit.case: new <slug> creates <name>.worktrees/<slug> whose path is canonical (realpath) and resolves as a sibling of the repo, not a string-equal but symlinked alias
the created branch carries branch.<slug>.remote == "." and branch.<slug>.merge == refs/heads/main (git config --get check)
an uncommitted design-slot file in the primary tree makes new refuse and creates no directory, no branch
with no [git] worktrees_dir key in .ai-engineering/config.toml the root falls back to <repo>.worktrees
with [git] worktrees_dir set in .ai-engineering/config.toml the worktree lands at that path
a second worktree declaring a file an open worktree already declared warns without blocking creation
list reports the open worktrees (slug and path) without mutating anything
rm <slug> removes the worktree and its branch and both disappear from worktree list / branch
no command the verb emits ever contains git push (read-only ahead/behind at most)

a slug with a space or a slash is rejected: new exits non-zero, creates neither the directory nor the branch, and prints the reason; the shape is enforced as a code rule (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$), not left to the agent
a well-formed slug is accepted: 'git-worktree-flow' and a slug mixing letters, digits, dot and hyphen each create the directory and the branch (the rule is not only negative)
no path or ref reaches git unquoted (cheap regression guard; unreachable while slug validation rejects separators)
a stale worktree entry whose directory was deleted out from under it does not crash list, and rm <slug> prunes it

not_tested: UI layer — feature has no UI; every checkpoint gate.ui is n/a.
API layer — no server, no HTTP endpoints, no DB (api layer empty).
Full `bun test` sweep — excluded in favour of the scoped specs above; sibling checkpoints iterate and the suite carries pre-existing unrelated failures.

The real end-to-end worktree lifecycle (a session builds inside a worktree, rebases on local main, merges --no-ff, cleans up) — this is prose an agent follows inside ai-orchestrator, not code; exercised by the behavior/review gates and the next build, not by a script.
The real ai-pr loop (push, gh pr create against main, CI/review watch, auto-merge) — needs live GitHub, credentials and a human decision; only the skill text and the pack presence are script-checked.
That no remote branch is ever deleted — proving it needs a live remote; the static checks cover only the skill text (no `push origin --delete`).
CHANGELOG.md gets its feature entry — written by the merge step per §08/§11, not by a checkpoint, so no checkpoint command asserts it.
AGENTS.md has no `Project config` section; unit commands are inferred from the `Build and test commands` line (`bun test`) and the neighbouring test plans.
